units.source_text: 从前津国有一女子，两个男子（菟原氏、智努氏）同样地热爱她。

en.t: Long ago in Tsu Province, there was a young woman whom two men, of the Ubara and Chinu families, loved equally deeply.

units.source_text: 其母难于解决，命两男子到生田川上射水鸟，射中者是女婿。

en.t: Her mother, unable to decide between them, ordered the two men to go to the Ikuta River and shoot at a water bird, saying that the one who struck it would become her son-in-law.

units.source_text: 一人射中鸟头，一人射中鸟尾。

en.t: One man hit the bird in the head, and the other hit it in the tail.

units.source_text: 女儿吟诗曰：“住世多忧患，投身愿自沉。

en.t: The daughter recited a poem: “Life in this world is full of sorrow, so I wish to cast myself in and sink.

units.source_text: 生田川水好，毕竟是空名。”

en.t: Though the waters of the Ikuta River are fair, in the end that beauty is only an empty name.”
Then she threw herself into the river and died.

units.source_text: 两男子也投身川中，一人执女子手，一人执女子足，三人俱死。

en.t: The two men also threw themselves into the river; one grasped the woman’s hand, the other her foot, and all three died together.
This story appears in The Tales of Yamato.
A similar story is also found in the Man’yoshu.
